input.body: Our team got 3,000 app reviews last month from the App Store and Play Store. Ops wants them sorted into bug, feature request, billing, and praise so the right people see them. Right now someone does it by hand every Friday. Also our onboarding flow is a mess and the new hire docs are outdated. Anyone have a good way to bucket feedback automatically?

Hey all, I run a small legal intake form for a family law practice. About 200 inquiries a week come in and I need to tag each one as custody, divorce, support, or other so the right attorney gets it. I tried a regex approach but it misses a lot. Our CRM is HubSpot if that matters. Budget is not a problem, we just need it working by end of month.

Is there anything out there that can label short text snippets with categories without training a model from scratch? We have around 50k product descriptions and want to tag them with one of 40 internal taxonomy codes. Our data team is two people and we've already burned a month on a homegrown approach. The CEO asked about it in standup today.

Rant incoming. Our Zendesk queue has 11 agents and most of the time goes to figuring out which team a ticket belongs to. Billing, technical, or account changes. Half the tickets are in Spanish too. Built a keyword router in 2019 and it's a disaster now. What do people use for this in 2024?

Been thinking about how to handle incoming security alerts from our scanners. We get maybe 40k findings a day across Snyk, Trivy, and Semgrep, and they all have different severity schemes. I want them normalised and tagged by team ownership. Not looking to replace the scanners, just the triage layer. Open to paid tools.

Content moderation question. We run a marketplace for handmade goods and sellers post listings with free text. I need to flag listings that mention prohibited items, medical claims, or counterfeit brands. Volume is about 15k listings a day. Our current approach is a keyword list that someone maintains in a spreadsheet and it's unmanageable.

Trying to classify inbound sales emails at our SaaS company. Reps get around 300 a day from partners, vendors, job seekers, and actual prospects. Only prospects should hit the sales queue. Our Outreach setup can't tell them apart reliably. Would pay for something that just works out of the box.

Anyone dealt with classifying government FOIA request text into exemption categories? We process a few thousand a year and each one needs to be tagged with the relevant statutory category before routing to the right records officer. Currently it's a paralegal reading each one. We have procurement approval for a tool if it's worth it.

We have a Discord community of 80k people and the mod team is burning out. Messages need sorting into spam, harassment, off-topic, and fine. I looked at a few bot options but most are just keyword filters. Looking for something that understands context and can be tuned by our mods. Happy to talk to vendors this week.

Our medical coding team codes clinical notes into ICD-10 buckets manually and the backlog is now six weeks. The notes are messy, abbreviations everywhere. Does anyone have a tool that suggests a category and lets a human confirm? We'd rather spend money than hire four more coders.

Quick question: what's the best way to triage GitHub issues automatically? We get about 400 a month on our open source project across bug, docs, question, and good first issue. Maintainers are volunteers and nobody wants to do it. The built-in labeler action is too dumb for us.

Our insurance claims intake has text descriptions from adjusters and we need to route each claim to property, auto, or liability. About 8,000 claims a month. We're using a rules engine from 2015 that breaks every time a new claim type shows up. Our IT lead has budget approved for Q3 if we find something credible.

Has anyone used a tool to categorise recruiting emails and resumes cover letters by role family? We're hiring for 30 roles across eng, sales, and ops and the recruiters are swamped. We have Greenhouse. Want something that tags the candidate pipeline before it reaches hiring managers.

Anyone else find their customer NPS survey free-text responses impossible to analyse? Thousands of answers per quarter. I just need themes tagged so I can count them. Sentiment alone isn't enough. Have a few options in mind but wondering what's actually worth paying for.

We are a logistics company and our dispatchers read every inbound freight quote request to determine lane type, hazmat status, and equipment needed. It's around 1,200 requests a day. Looking into whether any product can pre-classify these so dispatch only handles exceptions.

Built a little Python script with scikit-learn to tag support tickets but it's brittle and nobody else on the team understands it. Thinking about buying something managed instead. We have about 60k tickets historical data across 25 categories. Anyone have experience with a hosted option that handles retraining?

Our bank's compliance team has to tag transaction memo fields with reason codes for AML review. The memos are free text, super inconsistent, and volume is growing fast. The current vendor's tagger is slow and misses about one in five. What are people using for this in regulated environments?

Need to label thousands of podcast episode descriptions by topic for our recommendation engine. Right now we use a hand-maintained list of 300 tags and an intern. Searching for a service that can do multi-label classification with a human review step. We're a small team of four and this is eating our roadmap.

Customer success here. Every week I manually read through Gong call transcripts and tag which ones mention churn risk, pricing objections, or competitor evaluation. It takes hours and I miss things. Is there a tool that can flag these reliably across a few hundred calls a week?

Question for folks who run e-commerce returns. We get return reasons as free text like 'didn't fit' or 'arrived broken' and they're all over the place. I want them mapped to 12 standard codes so we can see trends. Shopify plus a homegrown spreadsheet right now. Would pay for a proper solution if it exists.

So I've been at this company about eight months now, and before that I was at a logistics startup in Leeds where we had a ridiculous amount of foosball and a cat that lived in the server room, which I still think about. Anyway, our finance team wants a weekly revenue number by 9am Monday and right now that number is assembled by hand: I pull three CSVs out of Stripe exports, a Google Sheet that someone's intern maintains, and a nightly dump from our Mongo cluster that I convert with a Python script I wrote in a hurry two years ago. Half the time a column gets renamed upstream and the script silently produces zeros. We have no real orchestration, just cron on an EC2 box that nobody wants to touch. What's the sane way to get these sources landing in the warehouse on a schedule with some schema checking, without me babysitting it every Sunday night?

Okay this is going to be a long one because I want to give context. We run a small marketplace, about 40 thousand active sellers, and our product catalogue lives in a legacy MySQL database that the old agency set up in 2016. Our search team uses Elasticsearch and they keep asking why inventory counts are stale. The answer is that the sync between MySQL and ES is a PHP script that runs every hour, and when it fails nobody gets told. Last month it failed for six hours over a weekend because a seller uploaded a title with an emoji that broke the encoding. We also have a Shopify storefront that needs the same inventory data, and someone wrote a second sync for that. Two syncs, two sources of truth, and I'm tired. We're trying to get a single change-data-capture style flow from MySQL binlog out to both targets with retries and a dead letter queue. Budget is there if the thing exists and works.

Hi all, long-time lurker, first real post. Background: I'm a data analyst at a mid-size insurance firm, been here four years, mostly Excel and SQL, and our IT team recently moved us onto Snowflake, which has been great apart from the fact that every claims file from our three regional TPA partners arrives as SFTP drops with slightly different layouts, different delimiters, and once a year someone sends a file in a totally different encoding. Right now I have a Windows scheduled task running a PowerShell script that copies them and a Python notebook that a contractor left behind. I'd like to replace that with something that handles the SFTP pulls, maps each partner's format onto our canonical claims table, and loads incrementally. We have a procurement window in Q3 so I'm starting to shortlist things now. Anyone have a sense of what's realistic for a team of two?

Pretty random tangent first: my dog got into the bin again and ate a whole sponge cake, which is why I'm up at 2am. So, back to the thing. We ingest clickstream events from our mobile apps through Kafka, about 3 billion events a day at peak, and we land them in S3 as Parquet. The problem is the downstream transformation into our sessions table is done by a Spark job that reads everything every time, because nobody built incremental logic, and it now takes 11 hours and our BI refresh has been missing its SLA for three weeks straight. I've been looking at whether a managed pipeline tool with incremental materialisation and built-in lineage could replace the Spark job and the Airflow DAG that babysits it. Our VP has said she'd sign off on spend above what we currently pay for EMR if it cuts the runtime to under two hours.

So we are a bakery software company, which is a weird niche, but we have about 900 bakeries on our platform and they all push point-of-sale data to us. Every one of them has a slightly different export format from their till provider, and our integration team spends roughly a third of their week writing one-off parsers. I've been asked to find a way to standardise the ingestion so that adding a new POS vendor is a config change rather than a sprint. We also need to push normalised sales and stock movements into the accounting packages our customers use, Xero and QuickBooks mostly, and that is currently also bespoke code per integration. I'm not looking for a generic iPaaS with a thousand connectors we will never use. I want something that handles file and API sources, schema mapping, and reliable delivery into those two accounting APIs, with retry and reconciliation. Engineering lead has the budget conversation next Thursday.

Right, so context: I've inherited a reporting stack at a university research group. Previous PhD student built everything in R scripts triggered by hand. Data comes from three sources: a REDCap instance for survey responses, an accelerometer export that dumps CSVs into a shared drive, and a lab LIMS with an API that rate-limits us to 100 requests a minute. Every time a new participant wave comes in, someone has to rerun the scripts in the right order and pray. We've got a grant renewal coming up and the reviewers want reproducibility and an audit trail of how each derived dataset was produced. I'm not a data engineer, I'm a postdoc who got stuck with this. We could maybe pay for a tool if it's not insanely expensive and doesn't need a platform team to run it. Any suggestions for getting from these sources to a versioned analysis dataset with lineage?

The actual issue: our team runs about 60 dbt models on top of Postgres, and we also have a handful of Python jobs that pull from partner APIs and write to the same warehouse. We have no visibility into which upstream table feeds which dashboard, and when a partner changes a field name the failure shows up as a broken Looker tile two days later. I'd like something that gives us column-level lineage across the dbt models and the Python ingestion, plus alerts on schema drift at the source. We're a 30-person company so I'm not looking for an enterprise procurement nightmare. I'd be happy to trial something for a month if it integrates with dbt Cloud and doesn't require us to rewrite the Python jobs.

Context dump before I get to it: our office moved to a new building in March and the wifi has been terrible ever since, which means half my Zoom calls drop. Anyway. I'm not the decision-maker but I've been asked to put together a shortlist of tools that can do CDC or scheduled extracts from SQL Server, Oracle and a Cerner feed, with monitoring that actually tells someone when it breaks.

We have a fleet of about 2,000 IoT sensors in cold storage warehouses, each pushing readings over MQTT to a broker, and a bridge service we wrote forwards them into a time-series database and also into a data lake for the ML team. The bridge is a Go service that one person wrote and that person has left. Messages occasionally get duplicated, sometimes out of order, and the lake copy and the TSDB copy drift apart by a few percent a week, which the ML team has noticed. What we need is a managed stream processing layer that can dedupe, reorder within a window, fan out to both sinks, and checkpoint so we can replay after an outage. Procurement threshold is somewhere around forty thousand a year. Happy to hear what people have used.

It's got Airflow, which I set up, and about 14 DAGs, half of which pull satellite and weather data from public FTP servers that are notoriously flaky.
